answer: Sybil resistance here rests on costly, non-transferable identity: each agent must bond an amount sized to the work it claims, and payout unlocks only after peers attest its output through a prism of independent checks. A falcon-style spot check randomly re-executes a slice of tasks, so one operator behind many clones cannot gain — the bond behind every extra identity becomes a liability the moment a check fails, and any delta between claimed and verified work triggers slashing. Fake identities therefore cost more than they can earn.
